newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank rejects VSZ bank acquisition plan.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank rejects VSZ bank acquisition plan.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it had rejected a request by steel producer VSZ a.s. to increase its holdings in commercial bank IRB.
"The NBS governing board on Wednesday rejected VSZ's request to allow an increase in its capital participation of bank IRB a.s.," an NBS statement said.
As of July 31, VSZ held 14.63 percent in IRB and any further increase could enable the VSZ to acquire control over the bank, the statement added.
IRB is included on a government list of strategic companies as well as being part of a group of banks that will undergo loan portfolio restructuring.
"VSZ as a potential shareholder did not present its own plan on participation in restructuring process in the bank," the NBS said in explaining its move.
The state holds a 35 percent stake in IRB through its privaitastion agency the National Property Fund (NPF).
The NBS statement did not make it clear whether the rejection would affect VSZ's current holdings in IRB.
VSZ's holdings in IRB caused a stir recently when it was recently revealed that it may have exceeded 15 percent, which by law needs central bank approval.
In August, VSZ asked for central bank permission to increase its stake in IRB, the third largest Slovak commercial bank, to over 20 percent.

Shortly after the request was filed, the Central Securities Registry (SCP) published figures showing VSZ already held some 20 percent of IRB, but later retracted the figures without further explanation.
VSZ Director Jan Smerek told Reuters earlier in the day that central bank approval "would make the whole situation at the bank more transparent".
He added that there were ways for VSZ to attain its goals even if did not have the central bank's blessing, though he did not elaborate.
VSZ is a major client of IRB, accounting for an estimated 1.5 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
